nodes.description:
Combined deficiency of the respiratory chain complexes that contain mitochondrially encoded subunits: complexes I and IV in the muscle of biopsied patients, with complex III also reported, alongside reduced complex I and IV subunit levels in muscle and reduced oxygen consumption in fibroblasts. The deficiency is tissue-variable: fibroblasts can be normal when muscle is clearly affected, and respiratory chain activities in muscle have been normal in some patients. Patient fibroblasts also showed raised reactive oxygen species production.

Conformance note: this node instantiates the primary_oxphos_deficiency module's central OXPHOS Complex Deficiency node, as a combined deficiency of the complexes carrying mitochondrially encoded subunits. The upstream Impaired Mitochondrial Translation node conforms to the module's Mitochondrial Translation Defect trigger.

nodes.description: Biallelic EARS2 variants reduce the function of the mitochondrial glutamyl-tRNA synthetase. EARS2 is a non-discriminating enzyme that charges mt-tRNA(Glu) with glutamate and also mischarges mt-tRNA(Gln) with glutamate, the substrate later amidated to Gln-tRNA(Gln). In patient fibroblasts and muscle the steady-state EARS2 protein level is markedly reduced for start-loss and destabilising missense alleles. Not every allele acts through abundance: the homozygous p.Gly317Cys variant of a fatal neonatal case left EARS2 protein levels normal, and structural modelling places it near the tRNA-binding surface of the catalytic domain. Aminoacylation by patient alleles was not measured in the cited studies.
